page: Microsoft Azure D1_v2 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a single dedicated x86_64 vCPU powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, with 3.5 GB allocated per core, and 51 GB of local storage. The CPU architecture supports instruction set extensions such as AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, but lacks AVX-512 and AMX capabilities.

In benchmark evaluations, the D1_v2 exhibits limited performance, consistently placing in the bottom 10% across all tested categories. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU benchmarks both score 741.48, reflecting the constraints of its single-thread, single-core design. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 60.99 GB/sec, which drops to 6.55 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and a write bandwidth of 4.81 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks are also limited, as evidenced by a Passmark CPU encryption score of 265.95 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 16.62 GB/sec.

Given its resource profile, the D1_v2 represents a low-cost, entry-level option suitable for lightweight workloads where high throughput and low latency are not critical. It is capable of handling basic static web serving at 0.89 GB/sec and lightweight Redis operations at 0.92 million operations per second. It can also run minimal LLM inference on very small models (135M parameters) at 36.72 tokens per second for text generation, though it lacks the capacity for larger models. This virtual machine is best utilized for development, testing, basic scripting, or low-traffic web hosting.
description: Microsoft Azure D1_v2 is an entry-level, general-purpose virtual machine in the Dv2 family, utilizing a single dedicated x86_64 vCPU from an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of RAM, 51 GB of local storage, and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Performance benchmarks place this instance in the bottom 10% overall, with a Geekbench single-core score of 774.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 1057.74. Memory bandwidth is limited, reaching 6.55 GB/sec for large uncached reads. Due to these hardware constraints, the D1_v2 is a cost-efficient option for non-production environments, basic development tasks, lightweight scripting, and low-traffic static web serving, but it is unsuitable for resource-intensive databases or complex multi-threaded applications.
